title: Latch and the Lost Keys
markdown:
Bright beams poked through Latch the rat’s burrow. Dawn broke. Birds chirped. Latch stretched until a buzz ran to his tail-tip. Today felt important. Big deeds. Brass goggles gleamed as he scampered out. Crisp air smelled of fresh bread.

Then — QUACK-QUACK. Dory. His duck friend’s quacks meant trouble.

He dashed to the canal, legs a blur. Dory paced the bank, feathers ruffled.

“Latch. Oh, Latch. Ghastly. A catastrophe.”

He skidded. “What is it?”

“My keys.” She pointed a webbed foot at the churning water. “House keys. The sparkly stone. Slipped while I practised my high dive. They’re floating.”

Latch squinted. The keys bobbed near the floodgate’s mouth. Through that gap and they would be gone. A key-tastrophe. Whiskers twitched.

“Don’t worry. Your engineer is on the case. I’ll build a raft.”

He scurried the bank like a workshop with legs. Twigs. Leaves. A strip of bark that had already been a boat in its dreams. Nimble paws lashed them with dandelion fluff. A snail offered advice Latch did not take. Zip, zap, tie, twist. Tiny, but he was proud. He tested it with a pebble; the pebble stayed, which he took as science.

“Hop on.”

Dory hesitated. The raft wobbled. “It feels… ticklish.”

“Steady. Reach. Don’t flail.”

She stretched. A flap sent a ripple. Whoosh — the raft tipped. Dory squawked onto the bank, soaked. The keys nudged faster toward the floodgate.

“Blast and bother. Too wobbly. Bigger. Better. Bolder.”

He dashed off, mind buzzing louder than the weir. Hollow reeds that whistled when he ran. A mushroom-cap deck, still smelling of woods. He wove a grass base tight as a promise and attached a maple-leaf sail with a knot his grandmother would have called showing off. This one looked proper. Serious engineering. Dory, dripping, saluted it with a soggy wing.

“A winner. I’ll guide it. No flailing.” He hopped on, tightrope-balancing. Wind caught the sail. The raft glided.

“Almost there. Genius.”

He manoeuvred close. He focused so hard he missed the river weeds. Thwump. Snagged. The keys drifted toward the grasping green.

“No. They’re going to be gobbled.”

Latch looked at the stuck raft, the keys, Dory’s face. No more building. He breathed.

“This is it. Exciting. Definitely daring.”

He twisted free of the snagged deck. The maple sail slapped, offended. Wind gusted as if it had been waiting to be useful. He saw his chance, a spark of the morning’s first buzz. He leaped, goggles glinting, an airborne missile, tumble and stretch, heart a drum solo. Canal-spray, weed-stink, the sparkly stone winking like a dare. The keys bobbed. He lunged. Snap.

Keys in his teeth, mid-air, a whisker before the weeds. He landed with a thump, metal jingling.

Dory rushed, quacking delight. “Brilliant, brave, magnificent rat. Best engineer ever.”

He grinned, dropped the keys into her beak. “A little zing and a boing.” Pride fizzed. Water, rafts, reeds: faced.

The sun climbed. Latch adjusted his goggles, a new sparkle in them. He and Dory, keys safe, raced toward town. Today, he decided, grinning so wide the goggles fogged, was going to be amazing. The canal kept chatting to itself. The floodgate, denied a snack, went on being a floodgate. Somewhere a high dive was going to be practised again, this time with the sparkly stone firmly on a string.
